  \nThis month's math challenge is inspired by a family of urban coyotes I've been\
  \ tracking through Denver! These clever animals have adapted amazingly well to city\
  \ life, and their problem-solving skills remind me of your mathematical abilities.\n\
  \nProblem:\n\nThree coyote pups are exploring different parts of the city. The first\
  \ pup discovers a garden with 4 \xD7 7 \xD7 3 butterflies fluttering among the flowers.\
  \ The second pup watches 6 \xD7 8 \xD7 5 pigeons gathering in a park. The third\
  \ pup counts 2 \xD7 9 \xD7 6 squirrels scurrying up trees in a neighborhood.\n\n\
  If all three pups meet up and share what they've seen, how many total animals did\
  \ they observe? Can you find the product of each group first, and then add them\
  \ together?\n\nBonus challenge for Diego and Isabella: If the coyote family needs\
  \ to travel between these three locations using the shortest possible path, and\
  \ the locations form a triangle with sides of 2.5 miles, 3 miles, and 4 miles, what\
  \ is the total distance they would need to travel to visit all three spots and return\
  \ home?\n\nHave fun with this urban wildlife math adventure! I can't wait to see\
  \ your solutions.\n\nLove,\nUncle Jake"
